requirements.requirement: Retain local administration and override permissions without registry credential authority
requirements.limitations: Source administrators receive sanitized registry id/name/endpoint/enabled values, not secret registry configuration. Browser confirms administrators cannot create Cyber overrides. A scoped Cyber user sees one authorized service and no administration link, and creates/revokes an exact-digest override. Actual HTTP pull and warm-cache denial independently verify those browser actions.

requirements.requirement: 100-image baseline, 23 replacements, 77 unchanged images, history and stable service identity
requirements.limitations: Fresh baseline and successor HTTP graph pulls each pass for all 100 images; all 123 distinct runtime variants executed successfully. Successor activation preserves service identity, retains exactly 77 roots, adds 23 and retires 23. All 23 retired roots receive release_superseded denials. Incomplete synchronization preserves the baseline; restored scoped registry content enables recovery. Successor pulls and override checks run with source Harbor unreachable and an initially empty blob cache; PostgreSQL manifest cache remains retained.

requirements.requirement: Atomic activation, failed-import rollback, replay, ordering, duplicate and concurrent import
requirements.limitations: Atomic rollback injects failure after native projection and before sealing/commit in SQLite and an actual PostgreSQL wrapper. Actual PostgreSQL also covers concurrent import. Actual target OCI graph faults and the live 100/23 incomplete HTTP synchronization preserve prior active state, then recover. No actual process-kill mid-activation was exercised.

requirements.requirement: Offline expiry, signed standalone revocation, rollback protection and cross-service authorization
requirements.limitations: Offline expiry is checked by direct authorization against persisted SQLite at one microsecond before, exactly at, and 365 days after the signed deadline, with upstream access forbidden. Two services sharing a digest cannot reuse an override in a direct SQLite authorization test. Actual target-registry graph verification imports a standalone signed sequence-3 revocation and rejects older replay; actual PostgreSQL separately covers revocation/replay. These are scoped automated/importer tests, not fresh live HTTP expiry or shared-artifact tests. An unreceived upstream revocation cannot be enforced offline.

requirements.requirement: Fixed or indefinite Cyber override with immutable scope, mission/risk acceptance and audit
requirements.limitations: Actual HTTP checks create fixed and indefinite overrides, pull the selected retired digest, audit use, deny the other 22 retired roots, revoke the grant and deny warm-cache reuse. An additional grant and its audit survive actual portal/database recreation and normal sync. Browser Cyber creates an indefinite grant, observes 11 audited uses and revokes it. Mission/risk acceptance and invalid scope/permission cases have automated coverage.

requirements.requirement: Immediate override revocation with cached bytes and concurrent authorization
requirements.limitations: Fixed, indefinite, post-restart and browser-created grants all deny warm-cache reuse immediately after revocation in actual HTTP checks. PostgreSQL tests cover both override-use/revoke lock orders. No new use is recorded after the persistence-test revocation. Revocation cannot withdraw already delivered bytes or terminate existing workloads.

limitations: This local qualification does not establish production readiness. Real deployment DNS/TLS, identity provider, trust distribution, resource sizing, backup/restore, monitoring and change procedures require staging qualification.

No seamless publisher-key rollover: fingerprint is part of service identity. A new key needs a controlled identity migration or separately qualified deployment; adding a trust pin alone is insufficient.

No fresh nginx scan was run. The actual prior source/hardened scan BOEs were independently downloaded from System A and freshly imported into System B. Synthetic rich, inventory and graph fixtures are separately labeled.

The source-approved ServiceImage row identifies prior patched digest eb007132ae918972f2de3ba02e45bc330460058472b13ba5fe4aa3e838c13663; latest scan overview identifies hardened digest 2dd3835ed3850194293bc9191b8a66504f66c069580b7c08dbe3e18200c33fa2. Import preserves this original discrepancy.
Actual nginx source relational policy_findings is empty; three observations reside in execution.raw_payload and remain retained. Native table count zero is not a claim of zero scanner observations.
Detailed Dockle alerts are separately retained original scan output, outside the original BOE evidence_documents list; signed captured observations and immutable target digest remain present.

Native public views expose a subset of original fields. Full context/BOE comparisons cover all captured fields; extension-only lineage/approval records and non-displayed inventory fields are available through release evidence/context APIs.
Browser trust store rejected the local test CA. Browser validation used loopback HTTP without weakening secure-cookie settings; authenticated API and registry checks used explicitly trusted TLS.

Target-local registry and a trustworthy local clock remain required. Disconnection from System A does not communicate future revocations. Revocation cannot retrieve previously delivered bytes or stop running workloads.
The supplied replica image includes an amd64 Cosign build; other architectures and other registry/referrer implementations require their own qualification.

Test runs overlap and must not be added. Early sandbox socketpair/connection failures were environmental; final successful reruns are cited. Initial broad stale assertions and remaining environment-specific skips are reported explicitly.

Expiry and shared-artifact isolation use controlled direct-authorization tests; signed revocation uses an actual registry graph importer plus separate automated/PostgreSQL coverage. No fresh live HTTP expiry/shared-artifact/revocation exercise or actual process-kill mid-activation is claimed.

Native Harbor attestation transport (.att) passes, including digest, original subject/predicate and signature preservation after source shutdown. Approved-release import/proxy currently authorizes signature (.sig) graphs only; integrated attestation graph routing remains Partial.

The broad command repeats two files, producing 34 duplicate passing executions: 1,169 passing executions correspond to 1,135 unique passing cases. Two exact PostgreSQL skips separately pass; the host encrypted-Cosign-key roundtrip remains unexecuted despite distinct actual Docker/Harbor Cosign coverage.
The disconnected pull starts with an empty blob cache while retaining the PostgreSQL manifest cache; this is not a claim that every cache was empty.

The deployed image and live browser/HTTP qualification predate the final retry-diagnostic correction: clearing a previous failure code before early disabled-source or registry validation. The 28-test focused sync/routes suite, including two new retry regressions, and final broad rerun verify the updated source. The graph quarantine ownership guard was also added after the live scenarios and passes 20 focused tests plus the final broad rerun. No repeat live deployment or fault scenario run is claimed for these last changes.
